Commit message:
add timeout parameter to to_dataframe and to_arrow met… (#2354)

### Description

This PR adds a `timeout` parameter to the `to_dataframe()` and
`to_arrow()` methods (and their corresponding `*_iterable`,
`*_geodataframe` and `QueryJob` wrappers) in the BigQuery client
library.

This addresses an issue where these methods could hang indefinitely if
the underlying BigQuery Storage API stream blocked (e.g., due to
firewall issues or network interruptions) during the download phase. The
added `timeout` parameter ensures that the download operation respects
the specified time limit and raises a `concurrent.futures.TimeoutError`
if it exceeds the duration.

Commit message:
add RetryBackoff spans for retry backoffs (#20715)

Adds OpenTelemetry tracing for the retry backoff sleeps in `run()` (HTTP
and gRPC transports).

For each backoff the client records a `RetryBackoff` child span of the
operation span, covering the sleep. The span is recorded once the sleep
ends, with its start time set to when the sleep began
(`trace.WithTimestamp`), so it is not visible while the backoff is still
in progress — a deliberate trade-off that keeps the hot path free of
span bookkeeping when the operation span is not recording.

A backoff cut short by context cancellation or deadline is still
recorded, so the trace shows the time sp
{"type": "feat"}

bare `u32` on it, because WASI metadata omits the permission bits and the

    let permissions = 0o755;

Commit message:
extract `runs.image` in Docker container actions (#47423)

When a GitHub Action uses a pre-built Docker container in its
`runs.image`, we didn't previously extract + suggest updates.

As Actions should really be digest pinning these container images, we
should make it easier for maintainers to keep these updated by
extracting + updating it.

We only need to extract this when there's a `docker://` prefix, and
ignore local i.e. `Dockerfile` references.

As the runner matches the `docker://` prefix case-insensitively[0], we
do the same, although this doesn't change the existing (case-sensitive)
handling of `uses: docker://...`.
